guides.title: Launch an application and focus the correct window
guides.summary: Reuse a matching visible window; resolve installed applications by friendly name when launch is needed.
preconditions: Know the requested application; distinguish multiple document windows by their observed titles.
procedure: For a known application, call launch_installed_app(query=friendly name or known .exe/.lnk path). It resolves, reuses eligible existing windows, focuses, and verifies readiness in one operation. Use its returned window_title for subsequent targeting.
If the task specifies a particular existing document/window, call list_windows and choose its observed title, then focus_window_advanced(title=that title).
Before typing, require interaction_ready=true from launch, or verified foreground focus. A process-only launch result is not ready for input.
verification: Check the returned window identity and foreground evidence; list_windows can confirm which window is foreground.
recovery: If launch returns DELIVERED or focus fails, inspect list_windows for the existing window or a blocking dialog before retrying focus. Do not relaunch a process that already started.
For an ambiguous app name, refine the query using known application identity; installed-app discovery is an alternative only if its tool is available.
pitfalls: Never treat process_verified alone as a usable window.
Do not use raw shells through the application launcher or guess installation paths.

guides.title: Type, append, or replace text in a desktop editor
guides.summary: Resolve a real editable control, write once, and verify its complete value without relying on caret position.
preconditions: The intended application window is known. Sending/submitting must be within the user's request.
procedure: Use ui_inspect(title=observed window title, control_type='Edit') or 'Document'; inspect names and editable state. Supply a unique target name or an observed scoped selector.

Call interaction_type(surface='desktop', text=desired text, title=window, target=editor). It prefers a writable UIA pattern and uses guarded Rust input only when supported and needed. replace=false appends; replace=true intentionally replaces the existing value. Keep submit=false for drafts.
Use submit=true only for an authorized submission. Do not enable focused_fallback to evade ambiguity or a rejected target.
verification: ui_type verifies the complete editor value. Its submit path also requires new post-submit evidence; text delivery alone is not a sent message.
For a known complete expected value, ui_wait_state(target=editor, title=window, state='text', text=expected) provides fresh exact readback.
recovery: On ambiguous or stale targets, inspect again and refine the editor. If delivery is uncertain, observe the current value/result before deciding what remains; never automatically resend.
If the editor lacks a readable or writable semantic pattern, use a separately available guarded input path with fresh observation.
pitfalls: Omitting target works only when the editor/composer resolves uniquely.
An editor's label is not its value. Text is limited to 4096 characters; multiline native fallback can be refused to avoid accidental submission.

guides.title: Fill or append to a browser field
guides.summary: Use an observed DOM editor and exact action readback; keep text entry separate from submission.
preconditions: The intended browser tab is selected and semantic browser access is available.
procedure: For an unsent typing request into the currently focused field, interaction_type(surface='browser', text=text) resolves a fresh focused editor and verifies its value without an extra model turn. It refuses uncertain focus.

For a named field, call browser_semantic_snapshot. Choose a visible enabled editor using target={node_id: observed id} with expected_version=snapshot version, or an exact resolvable role/name. Call browser_semantic_action(action='fill', target=editor, value=text) to replace, or action='append' to preserve existing text.
Only when authorized, submit with action='press', value='Enter' on a freshly resolved editor, or click the observed submit control. Keep the same observed frame_selector for iframe work.
verification: Fill/append verify the exact resulting value. For an additional known-value check use browser_wait_state with a stable role/name or observed unique selector, state='text', text=expected.
After Enter/click, wait for a meaningful destination or confirmation state; ACTION_EXECUTED is delivery evidence only.
recovery: Refresh the snapshot on STALE_UI or ambiguity. An error after input may mean the write happened: inspect or check the expected state before retrying.
Stop at BROWSER_ACTION_BLOCKED; human verification requires the user.
pitfalls: Snapshots omit field values and cover only the viewport. Do not infer an empty draft.
Waits reject node_id: use stable role/name or selector. Select controls require action='select', not fill.

guides.title: Click browser controls, navigate, and choose dropdown options
guides.summary: Choose actions from the observed control kind and verify the result that matters to the task.
preconditions: The selected tab/frame is correct; targets and intended outcome are known from current observation.
procedure: Snapshot the page. Click a visible enabled exact target using its node_id plus expected_version, or exact role/name when role_resolvable=true.
For input_kind='select', use action='select' and the known underlying option value. For a custom dropdown, click its opener, refresh the snapshot, then click the exact visible option.
For a checkbox use action='check' or 'uncheck' to request the desired state. After navigation, refresh the snapshot and verify destination content.
verification: Select/check/uncheck verify their local control state. Click/press need browser_wait_state on a meaningful destination heading, dialog, or result, using a stable exact role/name or unique selector.
Use state='hidden' only when disappearance is the intended outcome, not as proof that an unrelated destination loaded.
recovery: On target ambiguity, stale versions, or a changed frame, observe again and refine the target. After uncertain input, inspect the outcome before considering another mutation.
Human-verification blocks must be resolved by the user; do not change input backends to bypass them.
pitfalls: Snapshot labels are not native option values; snapshots do not enumerate those values. Never guess a value from its label.
Selected state or a successful click is not proof of completed navigation. Do not use node_id in browser_wait_state.

guides.title: Activate desktop controls by name, order, or relative position
guides.summary: Resolve exact UIA controls or constrained relative selectors instead of guessing coordinates or enumeration indexes.
preconditions: The window and control kind are known; parent/anchor names must identify real visible controls.
procedure: Use ui_resolve(title=window, target=exact label or automation id, control_type=observed type) for a named control.

For an ordinal, pass selector={ordinal:2,parent:{target:observed container}} and an explicit control_type. ordinal is one-based or 'last'; ordering is visible top-to-bottom then left-to-right within one container.

Other selectors support selected/focused booleans and adjacent={target:observed anchor,direction:'left'|'right'|'above'|'below'}. Inspect the resolved identity, then call ui_activate with the same targeting arguments.
After opening a menu, resolve its current item separately rather than carrying stale assumptions into the next action.
verification: ui_activate reports delivery; follow with ui_wait_state on a meaningful changed target. state='selected' checks SelectionItem state only, while state='text' verifies exact text.
recovery: If ordinals span containers or adjacency has ties, refine the parent, control_type, or exact target. Re-resolve after layout changes.
If activation may have happened, check the intended result before retrying.
pitfalls: Do not equate a snapshot array index with a visible ordinal.
Selection alone does not prove destination navigation. Hidden-state waits require an exact named target without a relative selector.

guides.title: Reuse, select, or open the requested Chrome tab
guides.summary: Keep browser work in the user's existing session and select the intended tab explicitly.
preconditions: Know whether the user requested an existing tab or an additional tab.
procedure: Call chrome_connect_cdp when no usable browser connection is established. Inspect session_type: existing-window supports guarded navigation/search but does not imply DOM access.
For a connected CDP session, call chrome_tabs and match the intended title/URL. Call chrome_use_tab(index=observed index), then chrome_current_tab to confirm context.
For an explicit additional/new tab, call chrome_new_tab(url=HTTP(S) URL or 'about:blank'). It reuses the existing Chrome window and can reuse a fresh managed blank placeholder.
verification: Check actual title, URL, and session context after selection. Tab creation must return verified page evidence; subsequent content work still requires its own verification.
recovery: Refresh the tab list when a tab closes or indexes change. If connection returns existing-window only, use available guarded search/navigation tools or request the missing supported connection; do not assume semantic access.
After uncertain creation, inspect existing tabs/window state before requesting another tab.
pitfalls: Tab indexes are zero-based and belong to the observed connected session.
Do not open a managed browser or extra blank tab merely to repeat an already available session.

guides.title: Search Google and optionally open the first result
guides.summary: Use the dedicated search operation to handle known search clauses in one bounded path.
preconditions: The user requested Google search; the query and whether to open the first result are known.
procedure: For search only, call google_search(query=the user's query). Set new_tab=true only for an explicit new/additional-tab request.
For search plus opening the first result, call browser_google_search_first_result(query=query). It resolves the first external result and excludes Google navigation/tracking/ad hosts.
Use preserve_search_tab=false to navigate the results tab; set true when the search results must remain open in their own tab.
verification: Inspect returned verification and the actual destination URL/title. A search result page alone does not fulfill a request to open its first result.
recovery: On a human-verification block, stop and let the user resolve it. After uncertain navigation, use an available read-only browser observation before repeating the operation.
If no valid external result is found, report that result or refine only as the user's request permits; do not invent a destination.
pitfalls: Do not separately search and click a guessed first link when the compound tool covers both clauses.
Do not treat a CAPTCHA or Google internal link as the requested destination.

guides.title: Scroll the browser viewport or an observed frame
guides.summary: Scroll in bounded increments, observe new controls, and stop when the viewport does not move.
preconditions: The intended tab is selected. For an iframe, its observed unique frame_selector is known.
procedure: Snapshot the current page/frame to record viewport position and visible targets.

Call browser_semantic_scroll(delta_y=bounded delta), positive to move down or negative to move up; delta_x supports horizontal movement. Each delta is between -5000 and 5000 and at least one must be nonzero.
Refresh browser_semantic_snapshot after movement, carrying the same frame_selector. Stop once the sought target is visible.
verification: Check before/after offsets and verified. at_boundary_or_not_scrollable=true means no movement; it does not prove that the desired content exists.
Newly visible controls need fresh targets/version before acting.
recovery: If unchanged, inspect whether the page is at its boundary, the wrong frame was chosen, or content lives in a nested scrollable control. Use an available control-specific path only after observing that container.
Stop at human-verification blocks.
pitfalls: This tool scrolls the selected document/frame viewport, not an arbitrary nested element.
Do not loop unchanged scrolls or reuse pre-scroll node versions.

guides.title: Scroll or use keyboard shortcuts in a desktop window
guides.summary: Bind input to the intended window/control and observe whether the requested content or state actually changed.
preconditions: The desktop window is identified; the intended pane and shortcut behavior are known.
procedure: Use ui_inspect(title=window) to identify the pane/control, then ui_focus(title=window, target=observed control) when a specific control needs focus.

For wheel scrolling, call desktop_scroll(clicks=small signed count): positive scrolls up, negative scrolls down. The pointer must already be over the intended scroll area; otherwise use an observed pointer-placement path if available.
For a known keyboard operation, call ui_hotkey(title=window, keys=key list), such as ['pagedown'] in a focused scrollable pane. Then inspect or wait for its intended state.
verification: Use ui_inspect(force_refresh=true) to see new controls or ui_wait_state for a known expected target/state. A delivered shortcut or 'Scrolled desktop' result does not establish application success.
recovery: If focus or foreground changes, stop and inspect the current window before sending more input. If content does not change, inspect pane focus, pointer placement, and boundaries.
After a shortcut with possible side effects, verify before retrying.
pitfalls: Desktop wheel signs differ from browser delta_y signs.
Do not send global shortcuts repeatedly or assume wheel delivery means the desired pane moved.

guides.title: Use fresh visual evidence for pointer movement, clicks, and dragging
guides.summary: Use vision for unlabeled or visual-only controls, translating the current image into physical desktop coordinates.
preconditions: Semantic/API targeting is insufficient; the intended foreground window is active and the target is visually unambiguous.
procedure: Call screen_observe and inspect its image, stable flag, foreground_hwnd, dimensions, scale, and virtual origin. Re-observe an unstable or changed scene.
Map an observed image point to desktop pixels: x=virtual_origin_x+image_x*desktop_scale_x, y=virtual_origin_y+image_y*desktop_scale_y; round to integers.

Use desktop_move(x,y) for pointer placement/hover, desktop_click_button(x,y,button='left'|'right'|'middle',clicks=1..3) for a known click, or desktop_drag(start_x,start_y,end_x,end_y,duration=0.05..2) for a known drag.
After a hover opens a menu or the layout changes, observe again before choosing another coordinate.
verification: Call screen_observe after input and inspect the application outcome. Pointer arrival or DELIVERED output alone does not prove an item moved, a menu opened, or a command succeeded.
recovery: If foreground, display geometry, or target changes, take fresh evidence and re-plan. If input may have happened, inspect the result before retrying.
pitfalls: Never use remembered/fixed coordinates, stale images, or browser viewport coordinates as desktop pixels.
Negative desktop coordinates can be valid on multiple monitors. Do not bypass browser challenge or permission guards with coordinate input.

guides.title: Inspect and complete native Open, Save, or confirmation dialogs
guides.summary: Inspect the actual foreground dialog and use its visible controls; verify the resulting file or application state.
preconditions: The intended native dialog is foreground. The requested operation, path, and overwrite intent are established.
procedure: Call dialog_inspect and check dialog title/class, visible enabled controls, and labels before mutating.
For a known field, call dialog_set_field(target=unambiguous observed title or class, text=value). For Open or confirmation, call dialog_click_button(target=observed intended button label).
For a standard Save As dialog with an unambiguous filename field and Save button, call dialog_save_file(path=destination inside JARVIS_WORKSPACE).
verification: Field setting verifies its text. Button clicking only reports delivery: inspect the resulting dialog/application state through available read-only tools.
dialog_save_file checks dialog closure and path existence. Verify saved contents separately with an appropriate available reader before claiming file completion.
recovery: On an overwrite prompt, error dialog, or save timeout, call dialog_inspect before another click. Resolve the actual state; do not blindly repeat Save.
If the dialog is custom, localized, or has several candidate fields, use an available semantic path after inspection instead of assuming standard Save behavior.
pitfalls: These tools act on the foreground dialog. A background dialog title is insufficient.
The save helper chooses the last visible editable control and a Save/OK-style button; file existence alone is not proof of new content.

guides.title: Execute ordered work and resume safely after interruption
guides.summary: Compile known actions once, retain durable step states, and resume the same immutable program without replaying completed or uncertain effects.
preconditions: An active mission exists. Each nested tool is exposed and its schema/targets are known; outcome checkpoints are available for delivery-only actions.
procedure: Call workflow_execute(workflow_id=stable id, steps=[{id,description,tool,arguments,checkpoint?},...]) for 1-32 known ordered steps. A checkpoint is {tool,arguments} using an allowed read-only state wait for the meaningful result.

After interruption or context loss, call workflow_status(workflow_id) to read the original program, statuses, and remaining steps. Inspect current application state with an available surface observation tool.
For a pending safe continuation, call workflow_resume(workflow_id) with the same id. Do not resend an edited program or restart completed actions.
verification: Check each step's actual result/checkpoint and the remaining list. Delivery-only steps need outcome evidence before completion.
recovery: For an uncertain attempted step, first obtain fresh successful observation after the action. Call task_verify(claim=precise claim, verified=true only when proved, evidence=observed result).

Call workflow_review(workflow_id,step_id,claim=the identical verified claim), then workflow_resume with the same id. Review rechecks declared checkpoints without replaying the mutation; if evidence cannot prove success, keep the step unresolved.
pitfalls: Raw coordinates, recursive/task calls, screenshots, and plain waits are excluded from workflow programs.
A failed or timed-out action can have taken effect. New workflow ids and changed programs must not be used to evade review or permissions.

guides.title: Edit active Word, Excel, or PowerPoint content through COM
guides.summary: Use supported Office APIs for precise content changes with immediate readback in the active document.
preconditions: Windows, pywin32, and an active supported Office COM application are available. The intended document and target are known.
procedure: Call wincom_inspect(application='word'|'excel'|'powerpoint') and confirm the active document/workbook/presentation matches the request.

For Word append text with wincom_word_append(text). For Excel call wincom_excel_set_cell(cell=A1-style address, value=scalar, sheet=known worksheet name), or omit sheet only when the inspected active sheet is intended.
For PowerPoint call wincom_powerpoint_set_text(slide_index=one-based index, shape_name=known actual shape name, text=value). The shape must support a text frame.
verification: Word verifies the resulting document tail; Excel verifies the cell's Value2; PowerPoint verifies the exact text readback. Inspect returned document/sheet/slide identity.
These tools do not save. If persistence is requested, use an available save path and separately verify saved content.
recovery: If no active COM application exists, establish the correct open document using available application tools before retrying.
For a missing sheet/shape or unexpected active document, inspect and correct identity. After uncertain append, observe the document before repeating it.
pitfalls: Inspection identifies the active file but does not enumerate PowerPoint shape names; never invent one.
Cell value readback is not formula-result verification. An in-memory verified edit is not a saved document.

guides.title: Navigate Discord conversations and enter or send text
guides.summary: Use dedicated Discord navigation to resolve conversation identity and verify the matching composer in one operation.
preconditions: Discord is open and ready. Distinguish selecting a conversation, writing an unsent draft, and sending an authorized message.
procedure: For an ordinal DM, call discord_select_chat(position=one-based visible conversation position). It excludes Friends/Nitro/Shop and verifies the selected conversation and composer.

For a named channel or DM, call discord_go_to(destination=exact name, server=known server when needed). If the request explicitly authorizes navigation and sending, discord_navigate_and_send(destination,text,server) performs both with context guards; all confirmation gates still apply.

For a draft, use interaction_type(surface='desktop',title=observed Discord window,target=observed composer,text=requested text,submit=false) after verified navigation. Never substitute a sending tool for draft entry.
verification: Check the returned exact route/conversation and matching composer evidence. Draft entry requires exact value readback; sending requires the dedicated send result and its independent outcome evidence.
recovery: If navigation partially executes or a send is uncertain, inspect the current conversation and outcome before any retry. Refine ambiguous names with the actual server context.
pitfalls: The first visible conversation is not the first arbitrary button in the UI tree.
Do not use generic Ctrl+K and guessed coordinates when dedicated navigation is available; never replay an uncertain send.

guides.title: Select a WhatsApp chat and enter an unsent draft
guides.summary: Select a visible WhatsApp chat with the dedicated ordinal resolver, then type through the verified editable composer.
preconditions: WhatsApp is open and interaction-ready; the requested chat position and exact text are known.
procedure: Call whatsapp_select_chat_native(position=one-based visible chat position,title=observed window title). It resolves UIA rows, uses the configured guarded input backend, and verifies selection or conversation-view change.

Resolve the current message composer from ui_inspect if its identity is not already known. Call interaction_type(surface='desktop',title=window,target=observed composer,text=requested text,submit=false).
Preserve any existing draft unless replacement was explicitly requested. Continue to the next task clause immediately after verified readback.
verification: Chat selection evidence is distinct from text evidence. Require exact composer readback for the requested draft; a focused row or successful click alone is insufficient.
recovery: If native typing refuses a nonempty editor or no input was dispatched, inspect the draft and use the semantic-capable interaction_type path. If delivery is uncertain, first observe and reconcile the current value; do not append duplicate text.
pitfalls: Never press Enter merely to verify a draft.
Chat order is the current visible list order, not an assumed contact identity; a later reordered list requires fresh resolution.

guides.title: Search, open, and verify YouTube playback
guides.summary: Use the existing structured YouTube operation for search, watch-page selection, and optional verified playback.
preconditions: The requested search phrase and whether playback or a new tab is wanted are known; the selected browser session supports inspection.
procedure: Call youtube_search_open(query=search phrase,play=true only when requested,new_tab=true only when requested). It reuses the selected tab by default, selects a real watch result, and checks video identity.
For the already selected video, use youtube_playback(action='status') to inspect, or action='play'/'pause' for the requested state; bind expected_video_id when known.
verification: An opened watch URL is not playback proof. For play requests require advancing video evidence and the selected video ID; for pause require the matching paused state.
recovery: If playback is blocked by an ad, unavailable inspection, or human verification, preserve the selected video and inspect status before retrying. Stop automated interaction with human-verification challenges.
pitfalls: Do not search again or create another tab just because playback failed.
A play-button click or page title alone does not prove that the requested media is playing.

guides.title: Use direct file tools and bounded terminal commands
guides.summary: Use workspace file operations for text and a noninteractive command only when a direct tool does not cover the task.
preconditions: The requested path and intended changes are known; applicable workspace instructions and normal tool permissions remain in force.
procedure: Use list_directory(path=workspace-relative or allowed absolute directory) and read_file(path) to inspect the target before editing.
Use write_file(path,content) for an authorized UTF-8 replacement or new file. It creates parent directories; it replaces the whole file rather than applying a patch.

When a command is needed, call run_powershell(command=explicit noninteractive command). It runs from JARVIS_WORKSPACE with a 60-second timeout. Quote literal paths and values correctly, and obey any required command prefix.
verification: Read the written file back and compare the expected content. read_file returns only the first 20000 characters, so it cannot prove a larger file is complete.
Inspect command exit_code and meaningful output, then verify the requested resulting state. A successful process exit alone is not universal proof of task completion.
recovery: On an error or timeout, inspect whether partial work occurred before retrying. Reduce scope or use a purpose-built available tool when appropriate.
If a path is outside the file tools' workspace boundary, respect the restriction; do not use the terminal to evade it.
pitfalls: Directory listings are capped at 500 entries; absence in a bounded result may be inconclusive.
Do not pass untrusted text as shell code, launch a shell through an application opener, or infer success from missing output.
